newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 9.0/10.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 9.0/10.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 9.0/10.0 percent on Thursday morning on the back of ample supply in the money market, dealers said.

But they said market focus was on Friday's liquidity which was anticipated to be tight on possible carry-forward effects from the past two Friday's, coupled with the month-end factor and weekly tax payments due Friday.
One local bank dealer said liquidity worry was reflected by sharp rises in tom/next swap rates to 3.0 points from 1.2/1.4.
"People were buying tom/next swap for rupiah funding on Friday. They are expecting tight condition tomorrow," he said.
Another dealer said fears over possible tight conditions were also indicated by rupiah tom/next deposit which was quoted at 15.0/20.0 percent against the usual 13.0/13.5 percent.
He said one-week money was last taken at 15.0 percent, compared with 13.25/13.75 percent in a normal day.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 8.32 percent against 9.89 percent on Tuesday.
